traits.central_spines_twisted.note: Britton and Rose's The Cactaceae (vol. 3, 1922, p. 38): '5 or 6 very stout centrals, curved and twisted, up to 7 cm long'; the Flora of North America (vol. 4, read on eFloras 2026-10-19): spines 'usually straight (curved and twisted in desert mountains and peninsular ranges of California)'. Read as often twisted, with the form's 'usually curved' already stated.

traits.spine_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), Echinocereus engelmannii: 'individual spines with broad zones of different colors: whitish or grayish, dull golden-yellow, or reddish brown to nearly black ... abaxial central spine often fading whitish'. With so many colours named, the colour was measured: the median of the non-green pixels inside the spine cover of eight iNaturalist photographs (imagekit batch inat-cacti-2026-10-19, photos 0, 1, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11 in key order), the brighter three quarters of each, then the median of the photos: RGB 155, 128, 112, a dull tan (the photos ranged from 135, 116, 112 to 183, 177, 166). Until 2026-10-19 the spines were coloured by hand and greyed over 10 years to a light grey, which drew a grown plant's spines white.

traits.stigma_colour.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) pp. 235 to 236, Echinocereus engelmannii: stigma deep green; a dark leaf green by hand.

traits.stem_colour.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) pp. 235 to 236, Echinocereus engelmannii: stems green (the spines extremely variable in colour, so they stay set by hand).

Anderson gives only the largest sizes; the typical ones, a little short of them, by hand.

traits.ribs.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), Echinocereus engelmannii: stems mostly erect, cylindric or somewhat tapering distally, (5-)14-45(-70) × 3-9 cm; ribs 10-13, crests slightly undulate. Britton and Rose (vol. 3, 1922, p. 38) gave 11 to 14, which stood here until round 5; the family's rule now spaces them so a grown stem bears the middle of the count, where until then a spacing of 2 cm set by hand fitted the count's least round every stem.

traits.tepal_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), Echinocereus engelmannii: flowers 6-9 × 5-9 cm; inner tepals bright rose-pink to magenta, proximally darker, 37-75 × (8-)14-25 mm, tips relatively thin, delicate.

traits.tepal_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), Echinocereus engelmannii: inner tepals 37-75 × (8-)14-25 mm, so 14 to 25 mm wide, 8 at the least; drawn by the family's rule as broad for their length as that, where until round 5 the funnel's share of the gap between thirty tepals drew them about an eighth as wide as long.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: an open clump of 5 to 60 cylindrical stems 10 to 45 cm tall and 4 to 9 cm thick, from the base, the outer ones leaning out and turning up. Magenta flowers burst from the sides near the stem tips in spring, followed by red, spiny fruit. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough stem heights from general knowledge: 15 to 20 cm by 15 years, about 30 cm by 30. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: 10 to 13 ribs hidden under dense spines, pale radials, two to six coloured centrals and a flattened lower central pointing down, all greying with age. Its flower, bud and fruit are drawn from its characters by the rules at Cactaceae and the flowering plants: tepals on a spiral, as many and as broad as the family's rules give, on a floral cup above the inferior ovary, its stamens, style and stigma lobes, and its fruit from its stated colour, size and surface. Until 2026-10-18 its flower and fruit looks were partly set by hand (round tepal tips, a centre and an accent colour by eye), and a look set by hand keeps the rule that gives it the year its months state from running, so it flowered and fruited all year.
